t.E948.agn: In 2025 EFSA re-evaluated oxygen and hydrogen together; stating that the two gases are of low toxicological concern as food additives and that dietary exposure is very low, it concluded that their use does not raise a safety concern. In the EU it is authorised at quantum satis (as much as needed) in all food categories, including foods for infants and young children; EFSA recommended some changes to the EU specifications.
t.E948.body: Oxygen is essential for life. Inhaled oxygen passes from the lungs into the blood; about 98.5% of the oxygen in blood is bound to haemoglobin in red blood cells and about 1.5% is dissolved in the plasma. In cells it is used by the mitochondria to produce energy.
t.E948.found.0: In the EU, may be used in many foods at quantum satis (as much as needed)
t.E948.found.1: As a packaging gas in packaged foods
t.E948.prod: A gas obtained by fractional distillation of liquefied air at low temperature (physical separation).
t.E948.regx.0: Re-evaluated together with oxygen and hydrogen; no safety concern, no ADI needed; changes to the specifications recommended.
t.E948.regx.1: Group I additive; generally authorised at quantum satis (as much as needed).
t.E948.summary: Oxygen gas. Used in fresh meat packaging to preserve the red colour.
t.E948.what: A gas used as a packaging gas and propellant.
